newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP and banks lift Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: BHP and banks lift Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened modestly firmer on Thursday, the market ignoring a third consecutive fall of the Dow on Wednesday, as BHP and major bank issues found buying support ahead of key wages data this morning.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 5.3 points at 2,352.0.
The December share price index was seven points firmer at 2,371 and at a 19 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market was warmed early by the stronger local bond market which lent confidence to speculation that wages data to be released this morning would induce a rate cut.
"The outlook for copper has continued to improve because of lower stocks. This is crucial for BHP at the moment," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.
The dealer said BHP's opening form breathed some life into early trade and sentiment was bolstered by the local market's defiance of a third consecutive fall on Wall Street.
"Interest rates are on investors minds, as is the likelihood of a Dow bounce tonight after the technology sector recovered last night," the dealer said.
Dealers said all the major banks opened higher ahead of wages data which is expected to support a monetary easing.
News Corp shares were amongst the strongest early, the stock rebounding from falls earlier this week after its ADRs found good buying interest in New York on Wednesday.
At 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT), News Corp shares were 17 cents higher at A$7.21 (US$5.72).

Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop opened slightly higher in line with the market, the company's stock showing little response to the news late on Wednesday that it had sold its troubled U.S. medical technology subsidiary, Telectronics Pacing Systems, for A$170 million.
The market awaits the debut of one of Australia's largest cotton production and ginning companies, Colly Cotton, which is due to commence trade at 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT).
